text: One day Tom took a shortcut through the swamp, a gloomy place where tall pines and hemlocks made it dark even at noon. <break time="0.8s" /> Moving as carefully as a cat, he picked his way along fallen tree trunks, for green moss hid deep pools of black mud. <break time="0.8s" /> At last he reached a firm piece of ground, where Native Americans had once built a fort during their wars with the first settlers. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting down on a fallen tree to rest, Tom poked at the soil with his stick and turned up an old skull from those wars. <break time="0.8s" /> Lifting his eyes, Tom saw a huge stranger sitting on a stump right in front of him, though he had not heard anyone approach. <break time="0.8s" /> The mans face was dark and dirty with soot, as if he worked among fires, and a heavy axe rested on his shoulder. <break time="0.8s" /> What are you doing on my grounds, growled the stranger, but Tom answered that the land belonged to Deacon Peabody. <break time="0.8s" /> The stranger pointed to a tall tree, which looked healthy on the outside but was rotten at the core, with Peabodys name carved on its bark. <break time="0.8s" /> Nearby lay another great tree, already cut down, which bore the name of Crowninshield, a rich man said to have made his fortune as a pirate.
